command: llvm-mc -triple=riscv64 -filetype=obj research/evidence/experiments/EXP-0098/pair-resolved.asm -o out.o && ld.lld -m elf64lriscv --image-base=0 -Ttext 0x1000 -o out.elf out.o && llvm-objcopy -O binary --only-section=.text out.elf out.bin
notes: Input (LF, trailing newline): `  .text` / `  lui a0, %hi(L1)` / `  addi a0, a0, %lo(L1)` / `  .space 0x22c` / `L1:` / `  .word 0`. `.text` is linked at 0x1000, so `L1` is at 0x1234 and the site of `lui` is 0x1000. Hand derivation: high half = (0x1234 + 0x800) >> 12 = 0x1A34 >> 12 = 1; low half = 0x1234 & 0xFFF = 0x234. The linked words are 0x00001537 and 0x23450513 (`37 15 00 00 13 05 45 23`), then 560 zero bytes to the 568-byte section. Both fixups are `resolve_in_place`, so no record is emitted; the section's `base_address` is load-bearing because `pc_reference_rule = none` cannot cancel the site. The bytes distinguish the rule from `pcrel_hi20`, which would write high half (0x1234 - 0x1000 + 0x800) >> 12 = 0, and from `identity`, which would write 0x1234 into the 20-bit field.
source: measured bytes from the linked image; RISC-V UDB `inst/I/lui.yaml` and `inst/I/addi.yaml` for the field placements
